classification.difficultyReason: Identify the height as opposite and the ground distance as adjacent, then apply sine and cosine directly to the given hypotenuse.

content.prompt: A ladder $8\text{ m}$ long standing on level ground leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ground. Calculate the following. Give non-exact lengths to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Vertical wall at left, horizontal ground and ladder descending to the right. Brick texture is omitted as contextual decoration.
spec.mathematics: The ladder is the hypotenuse labelled 8; the foot angle is 60 degrees; the wall and ground are perpendicular.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How high up the wall the ladder reaches.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the height reached, in metres.
$$\begin{align*}\sin60^\circ&=\frac{h}{8}\\h&=8\sin60^\circ\\h&=4\sqrt3\\h&\approx6.93\end{align*}$$
The ladder reaches $6.93\text{ m}$ up the wall.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the horizontal distance, in metres.
$$\begin{align*}\cos60^\circ&=\frac{d}{8}\\d&=8\cos60^\circ\\d&=4\end{align*}$$
The foot of the ladder is $4\text{ m}$ from the wall.
